land.text: the Lata region of southern Gujarat, which the dynasty 'ruled' as feudatories of the Western Chalukyas 'in their early years'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Western Chalukya'; Barappa is 'a general of Tailapa II'. The Chaulukya page, by contrast, has Lata under Chaulukya suzerainty in the 990s (Mularaja 'defeated the Lata Chalukya chief Barapa') and captured by the Kalyani Chalukyas 'before 1007'; the map keeps the land with those overlords (see notes).

land.text: Lata, which Karna annexed 'by 1074 CE'; the dynasty 'appears to have been vanquished by the Chaulukyas of Gujarat'

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Chaulukya dynasty'. The Lata land itself passed 1018 to the Paramaras (Bhoja), c. 1056 to the Kalachuris, and 1074 to the Chaulukyas in the other dossiers' ledgers.

rulers.name: Barappa
rulers.note: Page list: 'c. 970-990 CE', 'the dynasty's first ruler', a general of Tailapa II. The page spells the first and last reign years with 'c.'; the Chaulukya page calls him Barapa.

rulers.name: Gogi-raja (Gongi-raja)
rulers.note: Page list: c. 990-1010; he 'may have revived the family's rule in the Lata region'.

rulers.name: Kirti-raja (Kirtiraja, Kirtipala)
rulers.note: Page list: c. 1010-1030; a 1018 copper-plate of Kirtiraja was found in Surat. The Chaulukya page has Kirtiraja already defeated by Durlabharaja c. 1008, two years before this list begins his reign.

rulers.name: Trilochana-pala
rulers.note: Page list: c. 1050-1070; Nimbarka appears in the list without a reign.

correction.text: Lata proper, southern Gujarat: the Vadodara and Surat discs without the northern margin that Cliopatria keeps Chaulukya, the region the Chaulukya, Paramara and Western Chalukya dossiers use for the Lata events; the page's 'ruled the Lata region of present-day Gujarat'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The infobox gives no area and the page gives no boundary; the shape is the Lata proper region of the Chaulukya, Paramara and Western Chalukya ledgers, so the three agree. The dynasty held it as its own only for 1009-1017 on those ledgers (Chaulukya loss 1009, Paramara gain 1018); before 1009 the Chaulukya dossier has it Chaulukya (to 1007) and Western Chalukya (1007-1008), so the compiler will settle 970-1008 for the Chaulukyas (their predecessor-successor link) and the keyframe is a claim of the dynasty's seat, not of cells.

region.text: the Lata region of present-day Gujarat

ledger.note: c. 970: the Lata Chalukyas appear in southern Gujarat. Infobox 'Established: c. 970 CE'; they 'ruled the Lata region of present-day Gujarat during 10th and 11th centuries' and, 'in their early years', as feudatories of the Western Chalukyas; Barappa is the first ruler (c. 970-990). The page names no boundary and no capital; the Chaulukya page has Lata under Chaulukya suzerainty from the 990s, so this founding draws a dynastic seat, not land the Chaulukya dossier gives up.

c. 1009 (bridge): Kirtiraja takes Lata back. 'Kirtiraja regained control of the region within a short time, before being defeated by the Paramara king Bhoja' after Durlabharaja defeated him c. 1008 ('He invaded the Lata region, and defeated the Lata Chalukya ruler Kirtiraja (or Kirtipala)'). The page dates neither the recovery nor the end of Chaulukya hold; 1009 follows the Chaulukya dossier's loss of that year.

c. 1018: Bhoja subjugates the Chalukyas of Lata. 'Bhoja's first military aggression appears to be his invasion of the Lata region' (around 1018 CE); 'Bhoja subjugated the Chalukyas of Lata, whose ruler Kirtiraja may have served as his feudatory for a brief period.' The Bhoja page gives no later word on Lata.

region.text: Lata, vanquished by the Chaulukyas of Gujarat

ledger.note: c. 1070: the Lata Chalukya line ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1070 CE'; 'by 1074 CE, the dynasty appears to have been vanquished by the Chaulukyas of Gujarat'. The dynasty holds no land on the map after 1018 (Paramara, then Kalachuri, then Chaulukya 1074 in the other ledgers), so nothing changes hands in this year.

wars.name: Durlabharaja's invasion of Lata
wars.outcome: Durlabharaja defeats the Lata Chalukya ruler Kirtiraja c. 1008; Kirtiraja regains control 'within a short time'.
wars.note: The Chaulukya page dates Durlabharaja's accession ('c. 1008 CE'), not the campaign; the second year is the bridge of the Chaulukya ledger. No article of its own.

wars.name: Bhoja's invasion of Lata
wars.outcome: Bhoja subjugates the Chalukyas of Lata around 1018; Kirtiraja 'may have served as his feudatory for a brief period'.
wars.note: The page treats it as Bhoja's first military aggression; the date is 'around 1018 CE'.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier of the Lata Chalukyas; Lata is the shared region of the Chaulukya, Paramara and Western Chalukya ledgers.

sources.title: Chalukyas of Lata
sources.note: Identity, infobox c. 970-c. 1070, ruler list with approximate reigns, feudatory status, vanquished by 1074; silent on capital, Kalyani and Paramara events.

sources.title: Chaulukya dynasty
sources.note: Durlabharaja c. 1008 against Kirtiraja, Kirtiraja's recovery, Satyashraya before 1007, Kalachuris and Karna 1074; Barapa under Mularaja (undated).

sources.title: Bhoja
sources.note: Invasion of Lata around 1018; Kirtiraja a feudatory 'for a brief period'; silent on Lata afterwards.

notes: No Cliopatria row. The dynasty's own page (c. 970-c. 1070) and the other ledgers disagree on who held Lata: the page has it ruling Lata for a century, the Chaulukya page has Lata under Chaulukya suzerainty in the 990s, taken by the Kalyani Chalukyas before 1007, retaken by Durlabharaja c. 1008, recovered by Kirtiraja 'within a short time' and subjugated by Bhoja around 1018; the Paramara dossier then has it to 1056, the Kalachuris to 1074. This dossier gives the map what the cross-citing ledgers need: Lata proper as the dynasty's only 1009-1017 (Chaulukya loss 1009, Paramara gain 1018), and keeps the dynasty alive to the infobox's c. 1070 as the feudatory line. 970-1008 and 1018-1070 are overlord land on the map; the found and dissolve events are recorded for the state page, and a compiler conflict at 970 should go to the Chaulukyas (their predecessor link). Capital: the page names none (Bhrigukachchha appears only as a place Vigraharaja marched to), so identity.capitals is empty; a gap-filler should find a seat. Satyashraya's capture (before 1007) and Durlabharaja's 1008 attack are not on this page. Reign years are the page's 'c.' ranges. Wikidata id left null (unreachable).
